sampling_model.design: One consecutive trajectory in the fixed common path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) from a stationary regime \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\); identification is population-level and sampling uncertainty comes from temporal dependence.
sampling_model.units: Overlapping finite cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a)\) on the fixed product alphabet, indexed by their terminal time.
sampling_model.treatment: A hypothetical intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x)\); no experimental assignments are observed.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cylinder assignment in the fixed product alphabet has positive probability, hence every denominator cylinder used by the returned expression is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Probabilities of the returned \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders are estimated by empirical frequencies and their long-run covariance by the modified-Bartlett Newey--West estimator with \(h_T\to\infty\) and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives sufficient summary-graph front-door conditions and a common do-free expression for selected micro total effects under latent confounding.
The ID algorithm returns an observational functional or a hedge and is complete for a fixed finite ADMG.
Theorem 1.1 bounds the graph segment needed to decide identification for one fully specified periodic latent-confounded time-series graph.
A possible-c-component and region recursion is sound and complete for causal identification over the finite graph class represented by a PAG.
Fixing kernels and intrinsic sets characterize identifiable effects and nested constraints in a fixed ADMG.
Do-calculus is sound and complete for macro total effects in latent-confounded summary causal graphs.
A complete graphical characterization and two finite adjustment sets identify linear direct effects from summary causal graphs under no hidden confounding.
Under causal sufficiency, the paper gives summary-graph conditions and adjustment sets for singleton total effects.
Necessary and sufficient conditions and a pseudo-linear algorithm characterize identification by common adjustment in causally sufficient summary graphs.
Graphical fixing outputs can be compiled into weight-based and influence-function estimators under independent sampling.

body.tldr: The full sound-and-complete lag-robust fixing theorem is not established: a generic finite-role collision cannot be lifted by independent shifts without assigning several role values to one fixed-alphabet coordinate or enlarging that alphabet. The proved result is instead an explicit terminating three-way certified procedure. It returns a sound finite-cylinder identifying functional for the concrete outside-front-door witness and for every successful saturated ordinary-ID call when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free; it returns a direct positive stationary fixed-alphabet lag-switch countermodel pair on the verified binary collision; and it returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) elsewhere. Its transition bound is \(4+3^{n(\gamma+(n-1)L+1)}\). Every success supports the cylinder plug-in estimator and modified-Bartlett HAC delta-method interval under positivity, geometric beta mixing, the stated bandwidth regime, and nonzero long-run variance. EasyRCA ranks only certified successes and distinguishes a proved failure certificate from an unresolved abstention.

project_justification.gap: Existing SCG adjustment, linear direct-effect, micro front-door, macro do-calculus, periodic-graph ID, PAG, and fixed-ADMG results do not furnish a complete nonparametric decision rule for one lag-specific micro intervention uniformly over latent-confounded stationary refinements on a fixed alphabet. In particular, fixed-graph hedges do not automatically preserve time homogeneity, exact summary, positivity, equality of the entire process law, and the unchanged coordinate alphabets under a refinement switch.
project_justification.niche: The attainable contribution is certified partial identification with graph-native abstention. Acyclic directed summaries admit a finite saturated ancestral ADMG whose successful ordinary-ID output is uniform over refinements; a separate cyclic lag-switch construction proves genuine uniform nonidentification for the two displayed refinements, each of which admits its own refinement-specific identifying functional. The remaining cyclic cases require the still-open offset-sensitive normal form and direct fixed-alphabet witness construction.
project_justification.fill: The explicit ordered procedure recognizes one proved outside-front-door success, one proved positive stationary lag-switch failure, and otherwise makes a memoized ordinary-ID call on at most \(n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\) ancestral roles when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free. It outputs \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) whenever these certified rules do not decide the query. This yields sound success and failure implications, an explicit transition bound, a concrete whole-law collision, and HAC inference, without claiming the missing converse or enlarging \(\mathcal A\).

body.related_work: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Goessler, and Meynaoui study summary-graph total effects under causal sufficiency, while Ferreira and Assaad characterize linear direct effects under the same no-hidden-confounding boundary. Assaad gives a sufficient latent-confounded micro front-door result, and Ferreira and Assaad prove macro do-calculus completeness for interventions on whole summary clusters. None of those results supplies the direct fixed-alphabet stationary rejection construction needed for complete lag-specific micro identification. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman bound identification after one periodic fine graph is specified; Jaber and coauthors decide the finite graph class represented by one PAG; Shpitser and Pearl prove ID soundness and completeness for one finite ADMG; and Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser define the fixed-ADMG fixing operator together with reachable graphs and intrinsic sets. These fixed-input results motivate the finite acyclic branch but do not supply the offset-sensitive cross-refinement state invariant or the direct fixed-alphabet rejection construction requested by the open-ended question. The present proved comparison is therefore limited: the explicit two-coordinate query lies outside the defined front-door family and is identified by a displayed cylinder functional, but no universal inclusion of that family or embedding of Assaad's criterion is claimed. Viviano and Bradic motivate beta-mixing inference, Newey and West motivate the modified-Bartlett estimator, and the note derives the required finite-window CLT, HAC consistency, and delta method for the returned cylinder probabilities.
body.interpretation: A success tag is a positive causal certificate: the displayed arithmetic functional has the same value as the lag-specific intervention probability in every compatible SCM. A failure tag is a negative causal certificate: the supplied final SCM pair has the same entire observational process law but different intervention probabilities. An unknown tag is neither; it records that the current sound rules do not decide the query. This distinction prevents an unresolved graph from being silently converted into a zero or low anomaly-transmission score.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved step is not statistical. A finite rejection witness may contain several temporal roles of the same observed coordinate. Independent-shift replication then tries to place several role values into one coordinate-time variable, while product-slot or auxiliary-channel repairs enlarge the fixed alphabet. The proved procedure avoids this defect by constructing its only failure pair directly and returning unknown elsewhere. Strict stationarity and bounded structural lag also do not make the observed process finite-order Markov, so neither transition-kernel truncation nor semantic gluing of refinement-specific formulas supplies the missing completeness proof.
body.honest_scope: The note proves sound partial certification, not a sound-and-complete TID-SCG dichotomy. The acyclic saturated-ID branch is sound but not claimed complete for uniform identification; the static boundary returns unknown on ID failure; the front-door result is only the concrete outside-family witness; and the direct failure branch currently covers the verified binary lag-switch query. Completing all unknown cases, embedding the generic front-door family, and producing arbitrary direct fixed-alphabet countermodels remain open. The HAC theorem applies only after a sound success and additionally requires cylinder positivity, geometric beta mixing, the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).
